newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish insurer PZU shows PLN 90 mln loss in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Polish insurer PZU shows PLN 90 mln loss in 1996.

text.p: Poland's largest insurance company Powszechny Zaklad Ubezpieczen SA (PZU) had a net loss of about 90 million zlotys in 1996, against 105.2-million-zloty net profit in 1995, the company's deputy president said.

Ryszard Micyk told Reuters after a news conference on Wednesday the loss was largely due to heavy damages in motor insurance which amounts to 75 percent of PZU's overall insurance portfolio. But he said PZU was likely to show a profit in 1997.

He said that according to preliminary figures the state-owned insurer, which plans to start its privatisation this year with a new share issue, collected about 3.5 billion-zloty in gross premiums in 1996, up from 2.2 billion in 1995.
"According to unaudited data we had a 3.5 billion-zloty gross premium and a loss of 90 million zlotys...the forecast for this year is a 40-percent premium growth and a profit," Micyk said.
He also said the losses were caused by obligatory provisions which the company had to make and rising costs, due to relatively high salaries.
Micyk said the audited results should be ready by the end of April.
